test_title: PYST 8: SSC CGL 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 14th_September_2025_Shift_2)
subject: gk
question:
Consider the statements:

1. Every Money Bill is a Financial Bill.

2. Every Financial Bill is a Money Bill.

Which is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1: Every Money Bill is a Financial Bill** - This statement is **correct**.

 
 
• A **Money Bill** is a specific type of Financial Bill defined under **Article 110** of the **Indian Constitution**. It deals exclusively with matters like taxation, government borrowing, or expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
• Since a Money Bill is a part of the broader category of Financial Bills, all Money Bills are Financial Bills. However, the reverse is not true as not all Financial Bills are Money Bills.
 
• Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha has limited powers over them. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 2: Every Financial Bill is a Money Bill** - This statement is **incorrect**.
 
 
• While Money Bills fall under the broader category of Financial Bills, not every Financial Bill qualifies as a Money Bill. Financial Bills are classified into three types:
 
 
• **Money Bills (Article 110):** Exclusively deal with specified financial matters.
 
• **Financial Bills (Category A):** Contain provisions related to financial matters but also include other matters.
 
• **Financial Bills (Category B):** Involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India but are not classified as Money Bills.
 
 
 
• Unlike Money Bills, Financial Bills (Categories A and B) can be introduced in either House of the Parliament, and the Rajya Sabha has equal legislative powers over them.
 
• *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Only 1.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Money Bill (Article 110 of the Indian Constitution):**

 
 
• A Bill is considered a Money Bill if it contains provisions exclusively related to the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of taxes, borrowing by the government, appropriation of money from the Consolidated Fund of India, and other specified financial matters.
 
• It can only be introduced in the **Lok Sabha**, with the prior recommendation of the **President of India**.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** cannot amend or reject a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.
 
 
 
• **Financial Bills:**
 
 
• **Financial Bill (Category A):** Contains financial provisions similar to a Money Bill but also includes other matters. It can be introduced in either House of the Parliament.
 
• **Financial Bill (Category B):** Deals with expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India but does not qualify as a Money Bill. It can also be introduced in either House of the Parliament.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distinction Between Money Bills and Financial Bills:**

 
 
• **Money Bills:** Exclusively deal with financial matters listed in Article 110, require the President's recommendation, and have restricted Rajya Sabha powers.
 
• **Financial Bills:** Broader in scope, may include financial provisions but also other matters, and can be introduced in either House.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Money Bills:**
 
 
• The **Finance Act** of a particular year, which contains provisions for taxation and government expenditure.
 
• Other Acts directly related to government borrowing or expenditure.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Process:** The process for passing Money Bills and Financial Bills differs significantly, reflecting the distinct roles of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha in financial legislation.
